articles.title: A card payment that failed
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about a card payment that failed every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Open Settings > Billing; the failed charge is at the top with the reason given.
2. Fix whatever the reason says, usually by putting a new card on.
3. Press Retry to take the payment now rather than waiting.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

A failed payment is tried again after three days and then after a week. Nothing stops working before the second of those, and rotas stay readable even after it.

articles.title: Adding a second venue to the bill
articles.body:
The short version of adding a second venue to the bill is below. The note at the bottom is worth reading as well as the steps.

1. Open Settings > Plan and press Add venue.
2. Name it and give its town; it appears in the venue picker straight away.
3. The bill changes from the day you add it, worked out for the rest of the month.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

Adding a venue on Starter or Team moves you up to the Venue plan as part of the same step, and the page tells you what that comes to before you confirm.

articles.title: Changing the billing email
articles.body:
Changing the billing email comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Settings > Billing.

1. Open Settings > Billing and edit the address under Billing contact.
2. Save; invoices and payment notices go there from now on.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

The billing address is separate from any staff record, so changing somebody's staff email does not move the invoices, and this is where to look when they keep going to somebody who has left.

articles.title: Changing the card on the account
articles.body:
This is our page on changing the card on the account. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

1. Open Settings > Billing and press Change card.
2. Enter the new details; you may be sent to your bank to confirm.
3. Save, and the old card is removed at the same moment.

Whoever it affects is told by email, and the email says who made the change.

A new card is checked with a small authorisation that is released within a few days. It is not a charge, although it shows as one on some banking apps.

articles.title: Closing an account
articles.body:
A couple of the steps below depend on how your venue settings are set, so have those to hand before you start. The page is Settings > Plan.

1. Open Settings > Plan and press Close account at the foot of the page.
2. Type the venue name to confirm you mean it.
3. Export anything you want to keep before the date it closes.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

The account closes at the end of the month you are paid up to rather than that day, so there is time to change your mind and time to get your exports out.

articles.title: Getting a VAT invoice
articles.body:
The page for getting a VAT invoice is Settings > Billing. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Open Settings > Billing and fill in the company name, address and VAT number.
2. Save, then download the invoice you need.
3. Older invoices can be rebuilt with the new details from the same list.

Managers see the change straight away. Staff see it the next time they open the app or refresh the page.

If you look after more than one venue this is set per venue and is not shared between them, so it is worth doing at each site in one sitting.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

Rebuilding an old invoice keeps its original number and date and only changes the details at the top, which is what an accountant needs it to do.

articles.title: Moving down a plan
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about moving down a plan a dozen times in three days. Start at Settings > Plan.

1. Open Settings > Plan and choose the smaller plan.
2. The page warns you about anything the smaller plan cannot hold.
3. Confirm; the change happens on your next billing date, not today.

Everything here can be undone from the same page, so it is worth trying it out on a quiet day before you lean on it.

Nothing is deleted when you move down. A second venue on an account that drops to Team becomes read only rather than disappearing, and comes back if you move up again.

articles.title: Moving from starter to team
articles.body:
Here is what to do about moving from starter to team, step by step. You will find the page at Settings > Plan.

- Open Settings > Plan and press Change plan.
- Choose Team; the page shows what the rest of this month comes to.
- Confirm, and the extra is taken straight away.

Anything you change here goes into the account history with your name and the time against it, so there is always a record of who did what.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

Moving up takes effect the moment you press it, which is what you want when you have hit the starter limit and cannot add the person in front of you.

articles.title: Pausing an account over the winter
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about pausing an account over the winter a dozen times in three days. Start at Settings > Plan.

1. Open Settings > Plan and press Pause.
2. Give the date you want to start again; you can change it later.
3. Nothing is charged while paused, and it starts itself again on that date.

Nothing here happens overnight or on a timer. It is done when the page says it is done.

While paused, rotas and hours stay readable and nothing can be published. Staff can still sign in and look at what is already there, which suits a seasonal venue.

articles.title: Paying yearly instead of monthly
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about paying yearly instead of monthly every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

- Open Settings > Plan and choose Yearly.
- The page works out the year from your current staff count and takes off what you have already paid this month.
- Confirm; the next charge is a year away.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

A yearly account still counts staff every month, and a venue that grows a lot is billed for the difference at the year end rather than each month.

articles.title: Reading the charges on your statement
articles.body:
Reading the charges on your statement comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Settings > Billing.

1. Every line names the month it covers and the number of staff it counted.
2. Part months from a plan change show as their own line with the dates on them.
3. Compare the line against the invoice of the same date under Invoices.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

A month with a plan change in it has two lines rather than one, which is why a statement can show two charges in a month when nothing has gone wrong.

articles.title: Taking a venue off the bill
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about taking a venue off the bill every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Move or mark as leavers anybody who only worked at that venue.
2. Open Settings > Plan and press Remove against the venue.
3. Confirm; it comes off the bill on your next billing date.

Whoever it affects is told by email, and the email says who made the change.

The venue's rotas and hours stay readable afterwards and can still be exported. Nothing more can be published at it, which is what makes it safe to leave alone.

articles.title: What a plan costs
articles.body:
The short version of what a plan costs is below. The note at the bottom is worth reading as well as the steps.

1. Open Settings > Plan to see what you are on and what the others cost.
2. Starter is for one venue and up to ten people on the books.
3. Team is one venue and no limit on people; Venue is for more than one site.
4. Every plan is priced per month per active member of staff, billed in arrears.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

The page shows the price against your own staff count rather than a table, which is why two venues on the same plan see different figures.

articles.title: What counts as an active member of staff
articles.body:
This page covers what counts as an active member of staff from start to finish. It lives under Settings > Billing.

- The count is taken on the first of the month.
- Anybody not marked as a leaver on that day counts, whether or not they were rota'd.
- Leavers, and anybody added after the first, do not count until the next month.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

Somebody who leaves on the second of the month is counted for that month in full. There is no part month for staff, only for plans.

articles.title: Where to find your invoices
articles.body:
This article is about where to find your invoices. Everything below is done from Settings > Billing > Invoices, and you need to be a manager or the owner of the account to see the page at all.

1. Open Settings > Billing > Invoices.
2. Every month is listed with the date, the amount and the staff count it was based on.
3. Press the arrow at the end of a line to download it as a PDF.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

Invoices stay downloadable for seven years, including after an account closes, so there is no need to save them all somewhere else as you go.

articles.title: A payroll file that will not import
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on a payroll file that will not import. Open Hours > Payroll before you start.

1. Open Hours > Payroll and download the file you sent.
2. Check every line has a payroll reference; a blank one is refused at the far end.
3. Check the pay period dates match the period your payroll is expecting.
4. Rebuild the file and send it again once the records are right.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

Providers differ on the column order and on how they want dates. The layout is set per connection under Settings > Connections, and changing it there rebuilds the file in the shape they want.

articles.title: Bringing takings in from the till
articles.body:
Here is what to do about bringing takings in from the till, step by step. You will find the page at Settings > Connections.

1. Open Settings > Connections and connect your till system.
2. Choose which venue each till maps to.
3. Takings arrive each night and show on the wage cost bar the next morning.

A new till terminal is a new device to the till system, so it has to be mapped before its takings come through. Everything else keeps working while it is not.

articles.title: Calendar links and how they keep up to date
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on calendar links and how they keep up to date. Open Settings > Connections before you start.

- The link is live and always shows the rota as it stands.
- How often it is read is decided by your calendar, not by us.
- Force a refresh in your calendar if you need the newest week this minute.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

Some calendars only look once every few hours, and a few only once a day, so a rota published this morning can take until the evening to appear.

articles.title: Changing an API key
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on changing an API key. Open Settings > API before you start.

1. Open Settings > API and press New key.
2. Copy it before you close the window; it is not shown again.
3. Put the new key into whatever uses it, then press Revoke on the old one.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

It is worth writing down what you have set, because the next person to look after this will ask.

A revoked key carries on working for twenty-four hours, which is there so a nightly job does not fail overnight while you are asleep.

articles.title: Matching staff records between two systems
articles.body:
The page for matching staff records between two systems is Settings > Connections. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Open Settings > Connections and press Matching.
2. Names that agree on both sides are matched for you and shown with a tick.
3. Pick the right record by hand for anybody else, or mark them as not in payroll.

Managers see the change straight away. Staff see it the next time they open the app or refresh the page.

This is one of the few things an owner can do that a manager cannot, so it may need somebody else in the building.

Matching is by payroll reference first and by name second, so putting the reference on the staff record does most of the work before you open the screen at all.

articles.title: Putting the rota in a calendar
articles.body:
Managers ask us about putting the rota in a calendar more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Rota.

1. Open the rota and press Calendar link at the top right.
2. Copy the link it gives you.
3. In your own calendar, add it as a subscribed calendar rather than importing it.

Importing it instead of subscribing gives you a one-off copy that never changes again, which is the usual reason somebody's calendar is stuck on an old week.

articles.title: Reading a transfer error
articles.body:
The short version of reading a transfer error is below. The note at the bottom is worth reading as well as the steps.

1. Open Settings > Connections and then the transfer log.
2. Click the red line; the error is written out in full underneath.
3. Fix what it names, then press Send again against that run.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

Most errors are one of three things: a locked period, a member of staff who is not matched, or a pay period the provider has already closed. The log says which.

articles.title: Reconnecting something that stopped
articles.body:
This page covers reconnecting something that stopped from start to finish. It lives under Settings > Connections.

- Open Settings > Connections; anything that has stopped says so in amber.
- Press Reconnect and sign in to the provider again.
- Press Test, then look at the transfer log to see it go through.

It applies from today forward. Anything that has already gone through is left as it was.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

Connections are signed in as a person, so one set up by somebody who has left stops when their account at the provider does. Reconnecting as yourself is the fix.

articles.title: Setting up the payroll connection
articles.body:
Short answer on setting up the payroll connection: it is all at Settings > Connections, and the steps below take you through it.

- Open Settings > Connections and press Connect against your payroll provider.
- Sign in to them in the window that opens and allow the connection.
- Choose which venues it covers, then match your staff to theirs.
- Press Test to send one period through and read what comes back.

The change saves as you make it, and a confirmation runs along the top of the screen. If that confirmation does not appear, nothing has been written down.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

Anybody left unmatched is left out of every transfer without stopping it, so the matching screen is worth going through twice before you rely on it.

articles.title: Somebody who exists twice across the two systems
articles.body:
This article is about somebody who exists twice across the two systems. Everything below is done from Settings > Connections, and you need to be a manager or the owner of the account to see the page at all.

1. Open the matching screen and find the two lines.
2. Match ours to the one payroll is actually paying.
3. Mark the other as not in payroll so it stops appearing every time.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

The screen will not guess between two records with the same name, and it stops rather than choosing, which is why a married name and a maiden name can hold up a whole week's transfer.

articles.title: The nightly transfer and when it runs
articles.body:
Managers ask us about the nightly transfer and when it runs more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Settings > Connections.

- It runs at two in the morning UK time, every night.
- It sends anything approved since the last run.
- The transfer log lists each run with the rows sent and anything refused.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

Nothing that has not been approved is ever sent, so a week left unapproved on a Friday sits there all weekend and goes on the Monday night instead.

articles.title: Asking for time off from the app
articles.body:
Asking for time off from the app comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is the app, under You.

1. Tap You, then Time off, then Request.
2. Pick the first and last day, and choose full or half days.
3. Add a line about why if it helps, and send it.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

The screen shows what you have left before you send, but the figure does not come down until a manager approves it, so two requests in the same day can both look affordable.

articles.title: Clocking in from the app
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about clocking in from the app a dozen times in three days. Start at the app.

- Open the app when you get to work and tap Clock in on today's shift.
- Tap Clock out at the end, and tap Break if your venue asks you to record them.
- The shift shows the running time while you are on.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

Clocking in more than half an hour before the shift starts is refused, and the app says how long there is to go rather than just failing.

articles.title: Getting the app on a phone
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on getting the app on a phone. Open the app before you start.

- Look for Hollins Rota in the App Store or on Google Play.
- Install it, then open it and put in the email address your manager has on file.
- Allow notifications when it asks, so you hear about your rota.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

It needs iOS 16 or Android 10. Anything older can still use the website on the phone, which does everything except clocking in.

articles.title: Location and clocking in
articles.body:
People write in about location and clocking in most in the first week of the month, when everybody is publishing. The page is the app.

1. Allow location when the app asks, if your venue has this turned on.
2. The app checks you are at the venue and clocks you in.
3. If it cannot find you, use the tablet on the bar instead.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

Location is only asked for where the venue has turned it on, and a cellar or a back kitchen can be enough to defeat it, which is why every venue using it keeps a tablet.

articles.title: Notifications that do not arrive
articles.body:
Everything to do with notifications that do not arrive sits on one page, which is the app. You should not need to go anywhere else for it.

1. Check the app's own settings under You > Notifications first.
2. Then check the phone's settings for the app.
3. Turn off any battery saving mode the phone is applying to the app.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

Battery saving is the usual answer on Android, and it is set per app rather than for the phone, so one person on the team can be affected while nobody else is.

articles.title: Seeing your shifts for the week
articles.body:
Short answer on seeing your shifts for the week: it is all at the app, under Shifts, and the steps below take you through it.

1. Open the app; your own week is the first screen.
2. Swipe left and right to move between weeks.
3. Tap a shift to see its times, its break, its role and any note on it.

Weeks your manager has not published yet are not there at all, rather than being shown as empty, which is why next week can look blank on a Wednesday.

articles.title: Signing in on a new phone
articles.body:
The page for signing in on a new phone is the app. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Install the app on the new phone and sign in as usual.
2. Allow notifications again; the new phone asks on its own.
3. Sign out on the old phone, or ask your manager to take it off your account.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

You can be signed in on more than one phone at once. Signing out on one leaves the others signed in, which is why an old phone in a drawer keeps buzzing.

articles.title: Signing in to the app
articles.body:
If you are new to Hollins Rota, signing in to the app is worth understanding before your first busy week. Open the app and work down.

1. Enter the email address on your staff record, not a personal one you have not told us about.
2. Enter the password you set when you accepted your invitation.
3. Tap Forgotten password if you have never set one.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

The app and the website share one password, so changing it on one changes it on the other.

articles.title: Swapping a shift from the app
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about swapping a shift from the app a dozen times in three days. Start at the app.

1. Tap the shift you want to give away and tap Offer to swap.
2. Everybody free who does your role sees it and can accept.
3. Once somebody accepts, it waits for a manager to approve it.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

The shift is still yours until a manager approves the swap, so turn up for it if the approval has not come through by the time it starts.

articles.title: The app asking you to sign in again
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on the app asking you to sign in again. Open the app before you start.

- Sign in again as normal; nothing has been lost.
- If it keeps happening, check whether your email address was changed recently.
- Update the app, then sign out and in once on that phone.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

If you want somebody here to do it with you on the phone, the desk is open weekdays from eight until six.

A change to the email address on your staff record signs you out everywhere, so a correction made by a manager on Monday is felt by the phone on Tuesday morning.

articles.title: The app on an older phone
articles.body:
Everything to do with the app on an older phone sits on one page, which is the app. You should not need to go anywhere else for it.

- Check the phone is on iOS 16 or Android 10 or newer.
- If it is not, open the website in the phone's browser and sign in there.
- Ask your manager about the venue tablet for clocking in.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

The website does everything the app does apart from clocking in and push notifications, so somebody on an older phone still sees their rota the moment it is out.

articles.title: Turning notifications on
articles.body:
People write in about turning notifications on most in the first week of the month, when everybody is publishing. The page is the app, under You.

- Open the app, tap You, then Notifications.
- Turn on the ones you want: new rota, changes to your shifts, and shift reminders.
- Check your phone's own settings allow the app to notify you at all.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

Both have to be on. Turning them on in the app does nothing if the phone is still blocking them, and the app cannot tell that the phone is.

articles.title: Using the app with no signal
articles.body:
If you are new to Hollins Rota, using the app with no signal is worth understanding before your first busy week. Open the app and work down.

1. Your own shifts are kept on the phone and can be read with no signal at all.
2. Clock-ins made offline are held and sent when the signal comes back.
3. Swaps and time off requests need a signal and will say so.

An offline clock-in keeps the time you tapped it, not the time it reached us, so the hours are right even though the line appears in the list late.

articles.title: Approving the week's hours
articles.body:
We get asked about approving the week's hours in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

1. Open Hours and pick the week you are paying.
2. Work down the flags: open shifts, big differences and anything corrected.
3. Press Approve week when the totals look right.

The change saves as you make it, and a confirmation runs along the top of the screen. If that confirmation does not appear, nothing has been written down.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

Approving does not lock the week. It marks it ready and lets the payroll file be built; locking is a separate step and is the one that stops changes.

articles.title: Clocking in and out
articles.body:
People write in about clocking in and out most in the first week of the month, when everybody is publishing. The page is Settings > Pay.

1. Turn clocking on for the venue under Settings > Pay.
2. Staff clock in at the start of the shift and out at the end, on the app or the tablet.
3. A shift shows as running until they clock out.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

Clocking in more than half an hour before the shift starts is refused with a line on screen, which is the setting most venues want and the one nobody expects.

articles.title: Clocking in on the venue tablet
articles.body:
Everything to do with clocking in on the venue tablet sits on one page, which is Settings > Pay. You should not need to go anywhere else for it.

1. Sign the tablet in once as the venue under Settings > Pay, then leave it signed in.
2. Staff tap their own name and enter their four digit code.
3. The tablet shows who is on and who is due in for the rest of the day.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

The tablet keeps clock-ins on the device when the wifi drops and sends them when it comes back, so the times are right even though they appear late.

articles.title: Contracted hours and how to set them
articles.body:
Here is what we tell people who write in about contracted hours and how to set them. Start at Hours and work down the page.

1. Open the staff record and enter the hours under Contract.
2. Enter nought for somebody on no fixed hours; the warnings then leave them alone.
3. Save; the rota starts counting against the new figure from the next week you build.

Managers see the change straight away. Staff see it the next time they open the app or refresh the page.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

The figure is per week even where you pay monthly, because the rota and the warnings both work in weeks.

articles.title: Correcting last week's hours after payroll has run
articles.body:
Short answer on correcting last week's hours after payroll has run: it is all at Hours, and the steps below take you through it.

1. Check whether the period is locked; if it is, the correction belongs on the next one.
2. Add an adjustment line against the person with the hours and a reason.
3. It appears on the next payroll file as its own line rather than changing the old one.

Nothing here happens overnight or on a timer. It is done when the page says it is done.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

Tell whoever runs your payroll what the adjustment is for. The line carries your reason, but a note in advance saves them ringing you about it.

articles.title: Different rates at different venues
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on different rates at different venues. Open Hours before you start.

1. Open the staff record and open the Pay tab.
2. Add a rate against each venue rather than one rate for the person.
3. Shifts are costed at the rate for the venue they are at.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

Overtime for somebody working at two venues is paid at the rate of the venue where the hours took them over the contract, which is whichever shift came last in the week.

articles.title: Editing hours you have already approved
articles.body:
Here is what to do about editing hours you have already approved, step by step. You will find the page at Hours.

1. Open the week and press Reopen at the top.
2. Make the correction and say why in the box; the reason stays on the line.
3. Approve the week again.

The rest of the team carry on working while you do this. Nothing is taken offline.

Reopening is refused once the period is locked. At that point the correction belongs on the next period as an adjustment, which is what payroll will be expecting.

articles.title: Holiday pay and the twelve week average
articles.body:
We get asked about holiday pay and the twelve week average in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

1. Turn the average on under Settings > Pay.
2. It uses the twelve paid weeks before the holiday, skipping weeks with no hours.
3. The figure shows on the holiday booking and goes into the payroll file as its own line.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

Somebody who has been with you fewer than twelve weeks is averaged over what there is, and the booking says how many weeks it used.

articles.title: Hours worked against hours rota'd
articles.body:
A couple of the steps below depend on how your venue settings are set, so have those to hand before you start. The page is Hours > Week.

- Open Hours > Week; the two columns sit next to each other with the difference beside them.
- Sort by the difference to bring the biggest gaps to the top.
- Click any line to see the clock-ins behind the worked figure.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

Open cover shifts count in the rota'd column with nobody on them, so a week with cover still unfilled will always read as rota'd more than worked.

articles.title: Locking a pay period
articles.body:
Here is what we tell people who write in about locking a pay period. Start at Hours > Payroll and work down the page.

1. Open Hours > Payroll and press Lock against the period once payroll has gone.
2. Locked weeks cannot be reopened, corrected or rebuilt.
3. Only the owner can unlock one, and it goes on the account history when they do.

The change saves as you make it, and a confirmation runs along the top of the screen. If that confirmation does not appear, nothing has been written down.

Anything found after a lock goes on the next period as an adjustment line, which is why most venues lock the moment the file has been sent rather than at the month end.

articles.title: Missed clock-outs and how to put them right
articles.body:
Managers ask us about missed clock-outs and how to put them right more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Hours.

1. Open Hours; anything still running shows in amber with the word Open against it.
2. Click the line and type the finish time the shift actually ended at.
3. Give a reason, save, and the hours drop into the total.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

A shift left open never counts towards the week at all, rather than counting as a very long one, so the week reads low rather than high until you fix it.

articles.title: Overtime and how it is counted
articles.body:
Here is what to do about overtime and how it is counted, step by step. You will find the page at Settings > Pay.

1. Put contracted hours on the staff record; overtime is anything over that in a week.
2. Set the overtime rate under Settings > Pay, as a multiplier or a flat rate.
3. The overtime column on the hours page fills in as the week goes past the contract.

The change saves as you make it, and a confirmation runs along the top of the screen. If that confirmation does not appear, nothing has been written down.

Somebody with no contracted hours on their record has no threshold to pass, so they never show overtime however many hours they do.

articles.title: Rounding clock-in times
articles.body:
The page for rounding clock-in times is Settings > Pay. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Open Settings > Pay and choose the rounding, such as to the nearest five minutes.
2. Choose whether it rounds in the venue's favour, the staff member's, or to nearest.
3. Save; it applies to clock-ins from that point on.

The rest of the team carry on working while you do this. Nothing is taken offline.

If you look after more than one venue this is set per venue and is not shared between them, so it is worth doing at each site in one sitting.

Rounding is applied to the clock and never to the rota, so a rounded week can differ from the hours you rota'd by a few minutes even when everybody was on time.

articles.title: Sending hours to payroll
articles.body:
Everything to do with sending hours to payroll sits on one page, which is Hours > Payroll. You should not need to go anywhere else for it.

1. Approve the week, then open Hours > Payroll.
2. Choose the pay period and press Build file.
3. Download it, or let the nightly transfer send it if you have a connection set up.

Building the file twice for the same period gives you the same figures, not two sets. It is safe to rebuild it after a correction as long as the period is not locked.

articles.title: Setting hourly rates
articles.body:
The short version of setting hourly rates is below. The note at the bottom is worth reading as well as the steps.

1. Open the staff record and enter the rate under Pay.
2. Set the date it applies from; leave it as today for a rate starting now.
3. Save, and the wage cost figures redo themselves from that date forward.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

A rate that starts midweek applies from that day only, so one week can carry two rates for the same person and the payroll file shows them on two lines.

articles.title: The payroll file and what is in each column
articles.body:
This is our page on the payroll file and what is in each column. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

- The first columns are the payroll reference, the name and the venue.
- Then the basic hours, the overtime hours and the holiday hours, each to two decimals.
- Then the rate for each, and a line per rate where somebody had more than one.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

The payroll reference comes from the staff record and is blank until somebody puts it there. A blank reference is the usual reason a file is refused at the other end.

articles.title: Tronc and tips
articles.body:
This is our page on tronc and tips. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

1. Open Settings > Pay and turn Tronc on for the venue.
2. Enter the pot for the week on the Hours page, once the week is approved.
3. Choose how it divides: evenly, by hours worked, or by points you set per role.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

Tronc sits outside the wage cost figures and is shown separately, because the two are not the same money and reading them together makes the percentage look wrong.

articles.title: Wage cost percentage on the rota
articles.body:
The page for wage cost percentage on the rota is Settings > Pay. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

- Enter the day's takings by hand, or bring them in from the till.
- The bar along the top of the rota shows wage cost against takings for each day.
- Set the figure you are aiming at under Settings > Pay so the bar can colour itself.

It is wage cost before employer costs, so it reads lower than the figure your accountant works to. Most venues set their target a few points under to allow for it.

articles.title: Where the hours on a payslip come from
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about where the hours on a payslip come from every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Hours come from clock-ins where the venue uses them, and from the rota where it does not.
2. Open Hours and pick the week to see the two side by side.
3. Whatever is in the worked column when you approve the week is what goes to payroll.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

A venue with clocking half turned on is the one case that catches people: staff who clock have their worked hours counted, and staff who do not fall back to the rota, in the same week.

articles.title: Adding a shift to a rota you have already published
articles.body:
Adding a shift to a rota you have already published comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Rota.

1. Add the shift as you normally would; the week stays published while you do it.
2. The new shift shows with a dotted border until you press Publish changes.
3. Press Publish changes, and only the people affected are told.

The rest of the team carry on working while you do this. Nothing is taken offline.

The email that goes out for a change lists what changed rather than repeating the whole week, so somebody who picks up one extra shift is not sent their whole rota again.

articles.title: Approving a swap
articles.body:
Here is what to do about approving a swap, step by step. You will find the page at Rota > Swaps.

1. Open Rota > Swaps, or follow the link in the email.
2. Check the hours line, which shows what the week comes to for both people afterwards.
3. Press Approve, and the two shifts change hands and both people are told.

Turning a swap down puts it back as it was and tells both of them. It is worth writing a line about why, because the app shows your words to both sides.

articles.title: Bank holidays on the rota
articles.body:
The page for bank holidays on the rota is Settings > Rotas. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Set which bank holidays your venue observes under Settings > Rotas.
2. Observed days show shaded on the rota so nobody builds a normal week by accident.
3. Rota staff on as usual if you are trading; the shading is a reminder, not a block.

If two of you are in the same page at once, the last one to save wins, so it is worth saying out loud who is doing it.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

Marking a day as observed does not change anybody's pay. Bank holiday rates, if you pay them, are set under Settings > Pay and applied to the day separately.

articles.title: Building next week's rota
articles.body:
A couple of the steps below depend on how your venue settings are set, so have those to hand before you start. The page is Rota.

1. Open Rota and move to the week you are building with the arrows on the date bar.
2. Drag a name from the staff list on the left on to the day you want them on.
3. Click the shift to set the start, the finish, the role it counts against and its break.
4. Work across the week a day at a time; the totals under each column keep up as you go.
5. Press Publish when the week is right, and read the summary before you confirm it.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

This is one of the few things an owner can do that a manager cannot, so it may need somebody else in the building.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

A week you have not published yet is visible to managers only, so you can leave it half built overnight and come back to it. Staff see nothing until you press Publish.

articles.title: Changing the day your rota week starts on
articles.body:
This page covers changing the day your rota week starts on from start to finish. It lives under Settings > Rotas.

1. Open Settings > Rotas and change Week starts on.
2. Pick the day your trading week actually starts; most of our venues use Monday.
3. Save, and the rota redraws from that day.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

It is worth writing down what you have set, because the next person to look after this will ask.

Weeks you have already published keep the shape they were published in. It is worth making this change on a quiet week rather than the week before Christmas.

articles.title: Christmas and new year weeks
articles.body:
Christmas and new year weeks comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Rota.

1. Build the fortnight early and publish it in one go, so nobody has to ask.
2. Use a template saved from last year if the shape of your Christmas is the same.
3. Block the dates you are closed under Time off so nobody books them as holiday.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

Our own desk is thin between Christmas and the new year, so anything you want changed for the fortnight is best asked about before the third week of December.

articles.title: Copying last week's rota forward
articles.body:
The page for copying last week's rota forward is Rota. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Move to the empty week you want to fill and press Copy week.
2. Choose which week to copy from; it offers the one before by default.
3. Say whether to bring notes and open cover shifts across as well as the shifts.
4. Press Copy, and then edit whatever is different about this week before you publish.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

Copying into a week that already has shifts on it adds to them rather than replacing them, so a week copied twice ends up with everything on twice. Clear the week first if you are starting again.

articles.title: Getting back a shift you deleted
articles.body:
Getting back a shift you deleted comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Rota > History.

1. Press Undo in the toolbar, or Ctrl and Z, if you have not left the page.
2. If you have, open Rota > History and find the line for the deletion.
3. Press Restore against that line to put the shift back exactly as it was.

If two of you are in the same page at once, the last one to save wins, so it is worth saying out loud who is doing it.

Restoring brings the shift back but does not un-send the email that went out when you deleted it, so it is worth a word with whoever was on it.

articles.title: Giving somebody shifts at two venues
articles.body:
We get asked about giving somebody shifts at two venues in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

1. Open the staff record and tick both venues under Works at.
2. They now appear in the staff list at either site and can be dragged on to either rota.
3. Set their job at each venue separately if they do different work at each.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

Their contracted hours are one figure across both sites, not one each, so the warning about going over them counts everything they are on that week.

articles.title: Leaving a shift open for cover
articles.body:
Managers ask us about leaving a shift open for cover more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Rota.

1. Add the shift and leave the name blank; it shows as Cover needed in grey.
2. Add a note on the shift saying what it is for, such as covering sickness.
3. Fill it later by dragging a name on to it and publishing the change.

Whoever it affects is told by email, and the email says who made the change.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

Open cover shifts are counted in the rota'd hours for the week even though nobody is on them, so the wage cost figure reads high until they are filled or removed.

articles.title: Locking a rota so nobody else edits it
articles.body:
This article is about locking a rota so nobody else edits it. Everything below is done from Rota, and you need to be a manager or the owner of the account to see the page at all.

- Open the week and press the padlock next to the week heading.
- The week stays readable but nobody can add, move or delete a shift on it.
- Press the padlock again to unlock it.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

A week locked by one manager can still be unlocked by the owner, which is what to do when the person who locked it is on holiday.

articles.title: Moving a shift to somebody else
articles.body:
We get asked about moving a shift to somebody else in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

1. Drag the shift from one row to another, or click it and change the name in the box.
2. Check the warning line if one appears; it will tell you about a clash or a holiday.
3. Press Publish changes when you are done moving things about.

Managers see the change straight away. Staff see it the next time they open the app or refresh the page.

Both people are told: the one who has lost the shift and the one who has gained it. If you are moving several shifts, do them all before you publish so each person gets one email rather than four.

articles.title: Notes on a day of the rota
articles.body:
The page for notes on a day of the rota is Rota. It has changed a little since last year and this article has been brought up to date with it.

1. Click the date at the head of the column and type into the note box.
2. Use it for the things the shifts cannot say, such as a delivery or a private party.
3. The note shows to everybody at that venue, on the web and in the app.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

A note is not a shift, so nobody is emailed about one and it does not appear on the printed sheet unless you tick Include notes before you print.

articles.title: Offering a shift to the whole team
articles.body:
Managers ask us about offering a shift to the whole team more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Rota.

1. Click the shift and press Offer to team rather than putting a name on it.
2. Choose which roles are allowed to pick it up.
3. Publish, and everybody who qualifies sees it in the app as an open shift.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

An offered shift with nobody on it still counts towards the minimum staffing warning as unfilled, which is what stops one quietly sitting there until the day.

articles.title: Printing a rota for the back of house
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on printing a rota for the back of house. Open Rota before you start.

1. Open the week and press Print at the top right.
2. Choose Landscape, and tick Fit to one page if you have more than a dozen names.
3. Tick Hide rates unless the sheet is only going in the office.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

The printed sheet shows the week as it stands when you print it. If you publish changes afterwards, the sheet on the wall is out of date and nothing will tell you.

articles.title: Publishing a rota so staff can see it
articles.body:
If you are new to Hollins Rota, publishing a rota so staff can see it is worth understanding before your first busy week. Open Rota and work down.

1. Finish the week, then press Publish at the top right of the rota.
2. The summary tells you how many shifts are going out and to how many people.
3. Confirm it, and everybody with a shift that week gets an email and a push notification.
4. The week's heading turns from Draft to Published once it has gone.

It applies from today forward. Anything that has already gone through is left as it was.

If you want somebody here to do it with you on the phone, the desk is open weekdays from eight until six.

Anybody who has not accepted their invitation has no address to send to, so they are listed on the summary as not notified. Their shifts are still on the rota, and they will see them the first time they sign in.

articles.title: Putting a break on a shift
articles.body:
A couple of the steps below depend on how your venue settings are set, so have those to hand before you start. The page is Rota.

1. Click the shift and use the Break box to enter the length in minutes.
2. Tick Unpaid if the break comes off what the shift is worth.
3. Leave the start time of the break blank unless your venue fixes it.

A break longer than the shift is refused, and so is a break on a shift under four hours where the venue setting says breaks start at four.

articles.title: Putting a trial shift on the rota
articles.body:
Putting a trial shift on the rota comes up a lot with venues who have just taken a second site on. The page is Rota.

- Add the person to Staff first, with the job they are trying out for.
- Tick Trial on their record so they are left out of the bill until you keep them on.
- Rota the shift as normal and put a note on it saying who is showing them round.

Anything you change here goes into the account history with your name and the time against it, so there is always a record of who did what.

A trial shift still counts towards the hours for the week and still needs a break on it if it runs long enough, so build it the way you would build any other shift.

articles.title: Roles on a shift and why they matter
articles.body:
Short answer on roles on a shift and why they matter: it is all at Settings > Rotas, and the steps below take you through it.

- Set up the roles your venue uses under Settings > Rotas, such as bar, floor or kitchen.
- Pick a role when you build a shift; the shift takes its colour from the role.
- Filter the rota by role to see one part of the venue on its own.

If two of you are in the same page at once, the last one to save wins, so it is worth saying out loud who is doing it.

The role on a shift is what the minimum staffing warning counts, so a shift left with no role is invisible to it. Every shift is worth a role even when it seems obvious.

articles.title: Rota history and who changed what
articles.body:
We get asked about rota history and who changed what in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

1. Open Rota > History and pick the week you are asking about.
2. Every line has the time, the name of whoever did it, and what changed.
3. Press Restore against a line to put the rota back to how it was before it.

If you want somebody here to do it with you on the phone, the desk is open weekdays from eight until six.

It is easier on a laptop than on a phone, because there is more room on the screen.

History goes back a year. Restoring is itself a change and goes on the list, so there is no way to quietly undo something.

articles.title: Running rotas for more than one venue
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about running rotas for more than one venue a dozen times in three days. Start at Rota.

1. Use the venue picker at the top left to move between sites.
2. Each venue has its own week, its own templates and its own publish button.
3. Publish each venue separately so one site's staff are not told about another's week.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

It is worth writing down what you have set, because the next person to look after this will ask.

The staff list is shared across venues, so somebody can be rota'd at either. Their hours add up across both, which is why a clash warning can come from a site you do not manage.

articles.title: Saving a week as a template
articles.body:
This is our page on saving a week as a template. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

1. Build the week the way you want it kept, then press Save as template.
2. Give it a name your other managers will recognise, such as Summer week or Quiet week.
3. Choose whether it keeps the names on the shifts or just the shape of the week.
4. Apply it later from Rota > Templates on any empty week.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

There is a printer icon at the top right of this page if you want it on paper.

A template that keeps names goes stale as people leave. A template saved as the shape only never does, which is why most venues keep one of each.

articles.title: Sending a rota to a spreadsheet
articles.body:
This page covers sending a rota to a spreadsheet from start to finish. It lives under Rota.

1. Open the week and press Export, then choose the spreadsheet format.
2. Pick whether you want one row per shift or one row per person.
3. The file downloads with the venue name and the week in its name.

What you are looking at is live rather than a snapshot, so a refresh gives you the newest version of it.

If you want somebody here to do it with you on the phone, the desk is open weekdays from eight until six.

The export is a snapshot and does not update itself. Anybody working off it will be working off the week as it was the moment you pressed the button.

articles.title: Staff swapping shifts between themselves
articles.body:
Everything to do with staff swapping shifts between themselves sits on one page, which is Rota > Swaps. You should not need to go anywhere else for it.

- A member of staff opens their shift in the app and taps Offer to swap.
- The offer goes to everybody at that venue who is free and does that role.
- The first person to accept it takes the shift, and the swap waits for a manager.
- Approve or turn it down from Rota > Swaps, or from the email you are sent.

Everything here can be undone from the same page, so it is worth trying it out on a quiet day before you lean on it.

Most venues set this up in their first fortnight and then leave it alone from one year to the next.

Nothing moves on the rota until a manager approves it, so an unapproved swap leaves the original person still on the shift and still responsible for it.

articles.title: Stopping rota emails going out at night
articles.body:
Short answer on stopping rota emails going out at night: it is all at Settings > Rotas, and the steps below take you through it.

1. Open Settings > Rotas and find Hold notifications until.
2. Set a time in the morning, usually seven or eight.
3. Anything you publish after the evening cut-off waits and goes out at that time.

Anything you change here goes into the account history with your name and the time against it, so there is always a record of who did what.

The hold is for email and push only. A member of staff who opens the app at midnight sees the new week straight away, because the rota itself is already live.

articles.title: The warning when a shift goes over contracted hours
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about the warning when a shift goes over contracted hours every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Set contracted hours on each staff record first, or the warning has nothing to count.
2. Build the week as normal; the total under each name turns amber when it goes over.
3. Hover the total to see the contracted figure and the difference.

If two of you are in the same page at once, the last one to save wins, so it is worth saying out loud who is doing it.

It is worth writing down what you have set, because the next person to look after this will ask.

It counts the rota'd hours for the week, not the worked hours, so a week that ends up over because somebody stayed late will not have warned you when you built it.

articles.title: The warning when somebody is on twice
articles.body:
Here is what to do about the warning when somebody is on twice, step by step. You will find the page at Rota.

1. The shift shows a red corner and a line at the top of the column names the clash.
2. Click the warning to see the other shift, whichever venue it is at.
3. Move or shorten one of the two, and the warning clears on its own.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

There is no charge for any of this and it does not change what your plan costs.

The warning is a warning and not a refusal, because a shift in two halves with a long gap is a real thing at some venues. You can publish through it and it stays on the rota as a reminder.

articles.title: Unpaid breaks and how they come off the total
articles.body:
This is our page on unpaid breaks and how they come off the total. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

1. Set whether breaks are paid or unpaid for the venue under Settings > Rotas.
2. An unpaid break comes off both the rota'd hours and the worked hours.
3. A paid break is left in both, and the hours read the same as the shift length.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

Changing the venue setting does not go back and change weeks you have already published. Those keep whatever the setting was on the day they were built.

articles.title: Who is told when a rota changes
articles.body:
We rewrote this page after a busy first week of the month, when we were asked about who is told when a rota changes a dozen times in three days. Start at Rota.

1. Everybody with a shift that week is told when you first publish.
2. After that, only the people whose own shifts changed are told.
3. Managers at that venue get a copy of every change, whoever made it.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

Notes added to a day do not count as a change to anybody's shift, so nothing goes out for them. If a note matters, say so in a message rather than expecting the rota to carry it.

articles.title: A leaver who comes back
articles.body:
Here is what we tell people who write in about a leaver who comes back. Start at Staff and work down the page.

- Find them under Staff with the Leavers filter on.
- Press Reinstate and give the date they are starting again.
- Check the venue, the job and the rate, which are as they were when they left.

If two of you are in the same page at once, the last one to save wins, so it is worth saying out loud who is doing it.

Their holiday allowance starts again from the new date, and last year's booked days stay on the record as history rather than counting against this year.

articles.title: Adding a member of staff
articles.body:
People write in about adding a member of staff most in the first week of the month, when everybody is publishing. The page is Staff.

1. Open Staff and press Add.
2. Fill in the name, the job, the venue and their contracted hours.
3. Add an email address if they have one, or leave it blank and use a code instead.
4. Save; they appear in the staff list and can be rota'd straight away.

Nothing here happens overnight or on a timer. It is done when the page says it is done.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

The same page looks slightly different on the older layout. The buttons are in the same order, they are just along the top rather than down the side.

Somebody added on the first of the month counts towards that month's bill even if they have not accepted their invitation yet, because the count is of people on the books.

articles.title: An invitation that never arrived
articles.body:
We get asked about an invitation that never arrived in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

- Ask them to look in spam and in any promotions folder.
- Check the address on the staff record for a typo, which is most of them.
- If it is right, use a sign-in code instead and get them going today.

On a phone, turn it sideways. The columns fit much better that way.

Venue inboxes on shared mail systems are the common culprit, because the filter treats a message that looks like an invitation to somebody else as suspicious.

articles.title: Changing the email on an account
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about changing the email on an account every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Open the staff record and edit the address under Contact.
2. Save; a note goes to both the old address and the new one.
3. They sign in with the new address from that moment.

Anything you change here goes into the account history with your name and the time against it, so there is always a record of who did what.

Changing the address signs them out of the app on every phone, so it is worth warning somebody before you do it mid-shift.

articles.title: Documents that are about to run out
articles.body:
We get asked about documents that are about to run out in two or three different ways. The answer below is the one that suits most venues, and the note at the end covers the rest.

- Reminders go to the venue managers sixty days and thirty days before an expiry.
- Open Staff > Documents and use the Expiring filter to see them together.
- Upload the new document against the same record; the old one stays as history.

The change saves as you make it, and a confirmation runs along the top of the screen. If that confirmation does not appear, nothing has been written down.

This is one of the few things an owner can do that a manager cannot, so it may need somebody else in the building.

Everything here can be undone from the same page, so it is worth trying it out on a quiet day before you lean on it.

Nothing happens automatically on the expiry date. Nobody comes off the rota and no shift is refused; the record simply shows the expiry in red until it is dealt with.

articles.title: Handing the owner account to somebody else
articles.body:
Here is what we tell people who write in about handing the owner account to somebody else. Start at Settings > Permissions and work down the page.

1. Sign in as the current owner and open Settings > Permissions.
2. Press Hand over and choose a manager to hand it to.
3. Confirm from the email that arrives; the change happens when you follow that link.

If the page looks the same after you save it, refresh it once. Some browsers hold on to the version they already had.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

There is one owner on an account and the handover is not reversible from the new owner's side alone, so make sure it is going to the right person before you confirm.

articles.title: Inviting a member of staff by email
articles.body:
This article is about inviting a member of staff by email. Everything below is done from Staff, and you need to be a manager or the owner of the account to see the page at all.

1. Open the staff record and check the email address is right.
2. Press Invite; the email goes out within a minute or two.
3. The record shows Invited until they set a password, then Active.

Whoever it affects is told by email, and the email says who made the change.

If you look after more than one venue this is set per venue and is not shared between them, so it is worth doing at each site in one sitting.

An invitation runs out after fourteen days. The link then says it is no longer valid, which is the usual reason a new starter cannot get in on their first shift.

articles.title: Inviting somebody with no email address
articles.body:
If you are new to Hollins Rota, inviting somebody with no email address is worth understanding before your first busy week. Open Staff and work down.

- Leave the email field blank on the staff record and save it.
- Press Get sign-in code; a six character code appears on screen.
- They enter their name and that code in the app to set a password.

Every manager at that venue can open this, and so can the owner.

Nothing on this page is worked out overnight; it is right as at the moment you open it.

If what you are looking at does not seem right, check the date range at the top of the page first. Nine times out of ten it is sitting on the wrong week.

The code is good for seven days and for one person only. Write it down when it appears, because the page will not show you the same one twice.

articles.title: Keeping a manager to one venue
articles.body:
This page covers keeping a manager to one venue from start to finish. It lives under Staff.

1. Open the staff record and open Permission.
2. Untick every venue except the one they run.
3. Save; anything belonging to the other venues disappears from their screens.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

Only owners and managers can do this. A staff account can see the page but the buttons are greyed out.

A manager limited to one venue still sees staff who work at both, because they have to be able to rota them. They see only the shifts at their own site.

articles.title: Making somebody a manager
articles.body:
This is our page on making somebody a manager. The screens sit in slightly different places on a phone, but the order of the steps is the same either way.

1. Open the staff record and change Permission from Staff to Manager.
2. Tick which venues they manage.
3. Save; they see the manager screens the next time they sign in.

The rest of the team carry on working while you do this. Nothing is taken offline.

This is one of the few things an owner can do that a manager cannot, so it may need somebody else in the building.

Making somebody a manager does not change their pay, their contract or anything on the rota. It only changes what they can see and press.

articles.title: Marking somebody as a leaver
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about marking somebody as a leaver every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Open the staff record and press Mark as leaver.
2. Enter the date of their last shift.
3. Save; they come off the rota from the day after and stop counting on the bill.

Nothing here happens overnight or on a timer. It is done when the page says it is done.

Shifts already on the rota after their last day stay there until you take them off, showing as needing cover, which is deliberate so a week does not quietly go short.

articles.title: Resetting a password somebody has forgotten
articles.body:
Managers ask us about resetting a password somebody has forgotten more than almost anything else, so here it is in full. You will find it under Staff.

1. They tap Forgotten password on the sign-in screen and follow the email.
2. If they cannot get at the address, change it on their record first.
3. A manager can also press Send reset from the staff record.

It is worth a look once a week rather than only when something has gone wrong.

The reset link runs out after two hours, which is short on purpose. A link that has expired says so plainly and they can ask for another straight away.

articles.title: Right to work documents
articles.body:
This page covers right to work documents from start to finish. It lives under Staff.

1. Open the staff record and go to Documents.
2. Upload the document and give it a type and an expiry date.
3. The record shows a green tick once a right to work document is on file.

If you are not sure whether something saved, the account history under Settings lists the last ninety days with a name against every line.

Documents are visible to managers and owners only, never to the member of staff themselves, and they are kept for as long as the staff record is.

articles.title: Sending an invitation again
articles.body:
Short answer on sending an invitation again: it is all at Staff, and the steps below take you through it.

- Open the staff record and press Invite again.
- The old link stops working the moment the new one goes out.
- Check the address on the record first if the last one went nowhere.

You are asked to confirm before anything is changed for good, and the confirmation says in plain words what is about to happen.

This is one of the few things an owner can do that a manager cannot, so it may need somebody else in the building.

Everything here can be undone from the same page, so it is worth trying it out on a quiet day before you lean on it.

Sending it a second time to the same address that swallowed the first rarely helps. A personal address usually gets through where a shared venue inbox does not.

articles.title: Staff who work at more than one venue
articles.body:
A couple of the steps below depend on how your venue settings are set, so have those to hand before you start. The page is Staff.

1. Open the staff record and tick every venue they work at under Works at.
2. Mark one of them as their main venue; that is where their requests go.
3. Set a job and a rate for each venue if the two are different.

You can come back and change it later. Nothing on this page is set once and for all.

Everything here can be undone from the same page, so it is worth trying it out on a quiet day before you lean on it.

They count once on the bill however many venues they work at, because the bill counts people rather than places.

articles.title: What managers can see
articles.body:
This article is about what managers can see. Everything below is done from Staff, and you need to be a manager or the owner of the account to see the page at all.

- A manager sees the rota, the hours and the staff records for their venues.
- They can approve time off and swaps, and publish a rota.
- They cannot see billing, and they cannot change the plan or the card.

Give it a moment on venue wifi. The page catches up on its own and there is no need to do it twice.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

Wage costs are the line most people ask about: a manager sees them for their own venues only, and a shared report leaves out any venue they do not manage rather than refusing to open.

articles.title: Allowance in days and allowance in hours
articles.body:
People write in about allowance in days and allowance in hours most in the first week of the month, when everybody is publishing. The page is Settings > Time off.

1. Pick one under Settings > Time off; it applies to everybody at that venue.
2. In days, a booking takes a whole day off whatever length the shift would have been.
3. In hours, a booking takes the hours the person would normally have worked that day.

Hours suit venues where people work very different shift lengths, and days suit everybody else. Switching between them converts the figures using the contracted hours on each record, so those need to be right before you switch.

articles.title: Approving a holiday request
articles.body:
What follows is our answer on approving a holiday request. Open Time off > Requests before you start.

1. Open Time off > Requests, or follow the link in the email you were sent.
2. Look at the calendar strip at the top, which shows anybody else off that week.
3. Press Approve, and the days are blocked on the rota and come off the allowance.

Anything you change here goes into the account history with your name and the time against it, so there is always a record of who did what.

Approving time off over a week you have already published does not delete the shifts on it. They stay, marked as a clash, until you take them off yourself.

articles.title: Blocking dates nobody can book off
articles.body:
Two or three venues ask us about blocking dates nobody can book off every month, usually on a Monday. Here is what we tell them, in the order we tell them it.

1. Open Settings > Time off and add a blocked period with a first and last day.
2. Give it a reason, such as our busiest fortnight, so people know why.
3. Requests over a blocked period are refused as they are made, with your reason shown.

Managers see their own venues here. The owner sees all of them together.

Blocking dates does not cancel anything already approved over them. Have a look through what is already booked before you rely on a block.

articles.title: Booking a half day
articles.body:
If you are new to Hollins Rota, booking a half day is worth understanding before your first busy week. Open Time off and work down.

1. Book the day as normal and choose Half day instead of Full day.
2. Say whether it is the morning or the afternoon.
3. The rota shows the day as half shaded, so you can still put a shift on the other half.

Managers see the change straight away. Staff see it the next time they open the app or refresh the page.

A half day always takes half of the standard day off the allowance, even at venues counting in hours, which keeps the figures readable.

articles.title: Booking time off for a member of staff
articles.body:
